Container.Name: kodi-build-arm64-v8a
Container.Overview:
Cross-builds Kodi for Android arm64-v8a (64-bit) and signs the APK.
This container runs ONE build and then exits - a stopped container is the normal end state, not a crash. Watch the log; the finished APK is written to release/ inside the data directory.
Everything lives under a single data directory: src/ (the checkout, cloned on first run), state/ (Android SDK, depends prefix, Gradle home), release/ (the APKs) and keys/ (the signing keystore, which you put there yourself). Put it on a cache-only share - the build writes tens of thousands of small files and the array is slow for that.
Budget about 22 GB: roughly 14 GB of source tree once depends has built inside it, 8 GB of state. The first run additionally downloads about 3 GB of Android SDK and NDK, and rebuilds the whole dependency toolchain, so expect an hour or so. Later builds are incremental, typically 5-15 minutes.
With "Update from git" on, the loop is: push to GitHub, press Start.
The signing key is irreplaceable: without it an installed org.xbmc.fandangos can never be updated, only uninstalled and reinstalled. Keep a copy somewhere other than this machine.

Config.Name: Data directory
Config.Description: Holds src/, state/, release/ and keys/. Put the signing keystore in keys/ before the first build. Use a cache-only share.

Config.Name: Data root (container side)
Config.Description: Derives /data/src, /data/state and /data/release. Leave as is.

Config.Name: ABI
Config.Description: arm64-v8a (64-bit) or armeabi-v7a (32-bit).

Config.Name: Android package id
Config.Description: Package id baked into the APK. A different id installs alongside stock Kodi with its own data. Changing it changes which installed app the build can update.

Config.Name: Build configuration
Config.Description: Release, Debug or RelWithDebInfo.

Config.Name: Keystore file
Config.Description: Path inside the container. Put the keystore in keys/ within the data directory. If a file of the same name with .pass appended sits next to it, the password is read from that and you can leave the password field below empty.

Config.Name: Key alias
Config.Description: Alias inside the keystore. Checked with keytool before the build starts.

Config.Name: Keystore password
Config.Description: Leave EMPTY if you put a .pass file next to the keystore - that keeps the password out of docker inspect and out of this template file on the flash drive.

Config.Name: Key password
Config.Description: Leave empty if it is the same as the store password.

Config.Name: Git URL
Config.Description: Cloned when src/ is empty. Ignored once a checkout exists.

Config.Name: Git branch or tag
Config.Description: Branch or tag to build, and the branch the update below follows.

Config.Name: Update from git before building
Config.Description: 1 fetches and fast-forwards before every build, so pressing Start after pushing to GitHub builds the new commit. It refuses to build over local edits rather than discarding them.

Config.Name: Git remote
Config.Description: Remote to fetch from.

Config.Name: Discard local changes on update
Config.Description: 1 hard-resets to the remote branch every build. Untracked files are never deleted either way - the build tree lives inside the source directory.

Config.Name: Parallel jobs
Config.Description: make -j value. Empty means all cores.

Config.Name: Bundle BD-J JRE
Config.Description: 1 bundles the OpenJDK JRE and libbluray BD-J jars needed for Blu-ray disc menus. 0 produces a smaller APK with no disc menus.

Config.Name: Force reconfigure
Config.Description: 1 re-runs the depends configure step. Needed after changing the API level or depends build type.

Config.Name: Skip depends
Config.Description: 1 goes straight to the Kodi build. Only valid once depends has been built at least once.

Config.Name: Extra CMake arguments
Config.Description: Appended to CMAKE_EXTRA_ARGUMENTS.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User the build runs as. 99 is Unraid's nobody.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group the build runs as. 100 is Unraid's users.
